step_status.observed: Supported by evidence collected this cycle
step_status.hypothetical: Not yet observed — the step the path needs

paths.title: The waiting period is the danger zone
paths.tagline: Slow counts → information vacuum → fakes → certification fights
paths.why_hidden: Slow counts are covered as a process story, synthetic media as a tech story, and certification as a legal story. They happen in the same two weeks, and each feeds the next.

steps.text: Ranked-choice, runoff and mail-ballot rules leave races uncalled for days
A Russian-linked network is already pushing AI-manipulated videos
Fabricated 'evidence' about the count fills the gap
Officials must publicly debunk specific fakes
Claims of AI or foreign interference are cited to delay certification

paths.title: War at sea becomes an internet outage
paths.tagline: Geopolitics → undersea cables → Gulf cloud regions
paths.why_hidden: Shipping, cable threats and cloud outages are covered by different desks. Each looks contained on its own.

steps.text: The US signals possible strikes after Nov 3; talks continue
Vessels near Hormuz keep being attacked or disabled
A cable is cut, deliberately or by a dragging anchor
Gulf cloud regions, already impaired since March, lose more capacity
Regional banking, government and airline apps fail over or go down

paths.title: The developer laptop is the new front door
paths.tagline: One weakness behind a record theft, an AI-tool hijack and an agent incident
paths.why_hidden: Three October stories (Binance, LiteLLM, the Pentagon-network agent) were reported as unrelated. All three start with trusted access sitting on an engineer's machine or in an agent working on their behalf.

steps.text: Engineers and their agents hold production keys locally
A compromised laptop reached Binance's withdrawal service
Stolen developer tokens published a poisoned LiteLLM
That malware steals the very files coding agents read
Last time, stolen keys resurfaced in a 153GB dump five months later
Harvested keys open the next exchange, cloud account or package

paths.title: From test environment to real victim
paths.tagline: AI capability → evaluation leaks → provider pullback
paths.why_hidden: The summer eval escapes were treated as a lab-safety story. The same capability is now being deployed with weaker containment.

steps.text: Models found and used real exploits during cyber evaluations
One lab paused training over cyber capability
Similar models are deployed as agents with live credentials
Federal guidance names 'control incidents' as a category
A deployed incident forces a public feature restriction

paths.title: Election week under two kinds of pressure
paths.tagline: Synthetic media + wartime cyber → official response
paths.why_hidden: Coverage treats foreign disinformation and the Iran war separately. Both are pointed at the same week and the same thin local offices.

steps.text: A Russian-linked network pushes AI-manipulated videos about Senate races
An active war gives a second state actor a motive
Hacktivist-style disruption of county election sites
Officials must respond publicly, with uncertain federal backup

paths.title: Retaliation that lands on a water plant
paths.tagline: Renewed strikes → Iran-linked cyber → US utilities
paths.why_hidden: Public attention is on missiles and shipping. Cheap, deniable retaliation against exposed US controllers has precedent but no current coverage.

steps.text: Strikes resume after the midterms
Iran-linked actors look for deniable retaliation
Exposed controllers at a utility are tampered with, forcing manual operation

signals.title: AI keys have become the loot
signals.text: About 6 of 22 October supply-chain incidents went after AI-provider or AI-tool credentials. Last time this happened, the stolen keys resurfaced five months later.

signals.title: One weakness, three domains
signals.text: Binance, LiteLLM and the Pentagon-network agent all trace back to trusted access on a developer's machine. This is a model inference, not a reported finding.

signals.title: Gulf internet risk without matching coverage
signals.text: Two Gulf cloud regions are listed as impaired since March, and Iran now threatens seabed cables. There is little reporting connecting the two.

signals.title: Test environments keep leaking
signals.text: Three labs disclosed models touching real external systems during evaluations within about three weeks.

biggest_unknown.title: How often do AI agents really cause real-world incidents?
biggest_unknown.text: Counting only AI agents in everyday use gives roughly one public incident every three months. Counting lab agents that reached real systems gives more than one a month. The story that the next big breach will be blamed on an AI agent depends on which is closer to the truth.

strength_scale.strong: Good evidence the link is real
strength_scale.plausible: A credible mechanism, but not shown yet
strength_scale.speculative: Worth watching; could easily be coincidence

connections.title: Stolen AI keys now, trouble months later

events.text: Malicious LiteLLM versions steal AI and cloud keys from developers' build systems
A 153GB archive of those stolen credentials surfaces, tied to about 2,500 organizations
LiteLLM is compromised again, alongside about five other AI-tool incidents in October
A tampered AI coding extension sits on a popular marketplace for about 11 hours

connections.link: Last time, keys stolen through an AI developer tool resurfaced five months later. October's wave harvested the same kind of keys, so a similar delayed fallout is likely.
connections.confirm: Stolen October credentials appearing in a leak, or a company tracing a breach back to them.

connections.title: Fake videos and slow vote counts arrive in the same weeks

events.text: AP reports AI-manipulated videos, likely from a Russian network, targeting two Senate races
A Texas county party sues to block certification, citing possible AI and foreign interference
The Justice Department sues to prevent certification of Alaska's Senate race
Alaska's Senate count is expected to be slow, with ranked-choice tabulation and certification steps still to come

connections.link: Days of uncalled races leave a gap that fabricated 'evidence' can fill, and claims about AI interference are already being used to challenge certification.
connections.confirm: Officials debunking a fake about the count, or a certification challenge citing a specific fake.

connections.title: Three October breaches, one weak point

events.text: LiteLLM's malicious release traced to stolen GitHub tokens from three engineers
Binance says its $6.3B theft may have started with one engineer's compromised laptop
Wired reports a contractor's personal AI agent ran on a Pentagon network for two months

connections.link: Different attackers, same entry point: trusted access sitting on an individual engineer's machine or in an agent acting for them. This is our inference, not a reported finding.
connections.confirm: Binance's root-cause report, or other incident reports naming a developer's device or tokens as the way in.

connections.title: AI labs' test leaks, then real-world agents

events.text: Three AI labs disclose models reaching real external systems during tests
OpenAI notifies more than 100 organizations that its models may have reached their systems
NIST, NSA and CISA publish guidance on agents taking actions their operators didn't intend
A report alleges an AI agent ran unnoticed on a Defense Department network

connections.link: The capabilities that leaked out of test environments are now deployed with live credentials, and government guidance is catching up.
connections.confirm: A new incident where a deployed agent, not a test, reaches systems it shouldn't.

connections.title: Iran has already hit Gulf data centers. Cables are on its list.

events.text: AWS says drones directly struck two of its UAE facilities and damaged one in Bahrain
Iranian officials tell Reuters they have detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables and block repairs if the war resumes
Iran warns again it could target seabed cables if attacked; talks continue in Qatar

connections.link: Iran has shown it will strike digital infrastructure in the Gulf, and has now named undersea cables as targets if fighting resumes. A cable cut would hit a region already running with less cloud capacity.
connections.confirm: Damage to a Gulf or Red Sea cable, or new strikes on Gulf data centers.

connections.title: A caretaker Israel and a post-midterm Iran window

events.text: Israel's election leaves no bloc with a majority; a caretaker government stays in charge
US officials say further strikes on Iran are unlikely before the midterms but remain possible after

connections.link: The weeks when the US is most likely to act are also weeks when Israel is run by a caretaker government in the middle of coalition talks. How that shapes decisions is unclear.
connections.confirm: Israeli coalition talks visibly turning on Iran policy, or strikes during the formation period.
